How does a binary search algorithm work?
Binary search works by repeatedly dividing a sorted array in half. It compares the target value to the middle element: if they match, the search is done; if the target is smaller, it searches the left half; if larger, it searches the right half. This halving continues until the value is found or the search space is empty, giving it a time complexity of O(log n), far faster than a linear scan for large sorted datasets.
